title: Settlements (built-up areas)
summary: Outlines of every village, town centre and city in Maine, drawn by clustering building footprints wall to wall. Used at zooms 7-12, where the 925k footprints are too dense to draw.

inputs.name: src_overture.buildings
inputs.role: Building footprints (Overture Maps), clustered by their outlines.

inputs.name: src_census.cousub
inputs.role: Towns (county subdivisions): each settlement is named after the town holding most of it.

inputs.name: src_census.county
inputs.role: County name, joined through the town GEOID.

steps.title: Footprints in metres
steps.detail: Each building footprint, projected to UTM 19N (EPSG:26919) so distances are in metres. Its area is kept for the footprint_acres total.

steps.title: Cluster the footprints (DBSCAN)
steps.detail: Statewide ST_ClusterDBSCAN on the footprints themselves, so distance is measured wall to wall: a building joins a cluster when at least 4 buildings lie within 45 m of it. A school or mill counts by its walls, not its centre, so it no longer splits a neighbourhood. Buildings with no such neighbours are not part of any settlement.
steps.math: p \text{ is a core building} \iff \bigl|\{\, q : d(p, q) \le \varepsilon \,\}\bigr| \ge k, \quad d(p,q) = \min_{x \in p,\, y \in q} \lVert x - y \rVert,\ \varepsilon = 45\ \text{m},\ k = 4

steps.title: Close each cluster into a shape
steps.detail: Buffer the cluster's footprints out 45 m, then back in 35 m. The outward buffer fills the gaps between buildings; the inward one pulls the edge back to about 10 m beyond the outermost walls.

steps.title: Dissolve touching shapes
steps.detail: Shapes that touch or overlap are merged into one settlement (a second DBSCAN with distance 0). This joins a city split by parking lots and highways wider than the cluster distance. Settlements with fewer than 10 buildings are dropped.

steps.title: Attach large buildings at the edge
steps.detail: A building of 2,000 m² or more that is still outside every settlement but within 100 m of one is joined to the nearest: a local closing (60 m) around the building and the nearby part of the settlement, plus a 30 m-wide bridge along the shortest line between them, so the settlement stays in one piece. Large buildings further out (a lone mill, warehouse or farm complex) stay outside by design.
steps.math: S' = S \cup P \cup \Bigl(\bigl(P \cup (S \cap P \oplus B(150\ \text{m}))\bigr) \bullet B(60\ \text{m})\Bigr) \cup \overline{PS} \oplus B(15\ \text{m})

steps.title: Fill small holes
steps.detail: Gaps between building clusters (parking lots, school fields, a block of lawns) leave holes inside a settlement, which made larger towns look like swiss cheese. Every hole smaller than 10 acres, or 3 % of the settlement's area if that is larger, is filled; bigger holes (large parks, ponds, river corridors) stay.
steps.math: \text{fill hole } h \text{ of } S \iff A(h) < \max\bigl(10\ \text{acres},\ 0.03\, A(S)\bigr)

steps.title: Simplify, name and classify
steps.detail: Simplified to 5 m (topology preserved). Town = the town containing a point on the settlement's surface. Size class from the building count.
steps.math: \text{class}(n) = \begin{cases} \text{City or large town} & n \ge 1000 \\ \text{Town centre} & 250 \le n < 1000 \\ \text{Village} & 50 \le n < 250 \\ \text{Hamlet} & 10 \le n < 50 \end{cases}

parameters.name: Neighbour distance (DBSCAN eps)
parameters.why: The old centre-to-centre 58 m less the median house width (11 m), so ordinary neighbourhoods cluster as before while large buildings are measured by their walls. Tested on Androscoggin County: about the same settlements (302 vs 305) and area (+3 %).

parameters.name: Minimum neighbours (DBSCAN minpoints)
parameters.why: Keeps a farmhouse with a barn and two sheds from seeding a cluster.

parameters.name: Buffer out / in
parameters.why: Out must reach half the neighbour distance so neighbours' buffers join; the net 10 m beyond the walls keeps yards inside the outline.

parameters.name: Large building / attach distance
parameters.why: Schools, mills, plants and big-box stores at the edge of town; 100 m spans a parking lot or a road with its verges, but not open country.

parameters.name: Closing radius / bridge width
parameters.why: 60 m closes any gap up to the 100 m attach distance with a smooth edge; the bridge guarantees one piece where the closing alone would not.

parameters.name: Hole-filling threshold
parameters.why: Before this step 90 % of the 1,236 holes were under 10 acres (median 1-2 acres): noise from the closing step. Scaling with the settlement lets a city absorb parking lots and fields up to about 45 acres while a large park or pond still shows.

parameters.name: Simplify tolerance
parameters.why: Below a pixel at zoom 12; cuts vertex count for tiles.

parameters.name: Minimum settlement size
parameters.why: Below this the shape is a cluster of outbuildings, not a place.

parameters.name: Size classes
parameters.why: Separates cities, service towns, villages and hamlets.

caveats: Scattered rural houses are not in any settlement by design, so the buildings in settlements are well below the footprint count.
Large buildings more than 100 m from a settlement (a lone mill, warehouse or farm complex) stay outside.
A settlement spanning two towns is named after one of them only.
acres is the outline's area; footprint_acres is the area of the buildings themselves.

Rebuilt only when the number of building footprints or the method version (in the SQL) changes, about five minutes. An Overture update that keeps the same count is not picked up; to force a rebuild run TRUNCATE src_units.settlements_meta, then ./mapgen apply maine-places.

Method history: v1 clustered one point per building (58 m, buffer 60/-35 m); large buildings were measured from their centre, which split towns around schools and mills and left 91 % of buildings over 5,000 m² outside every settlement.
Small parks, cemeteries and fields inside a settlement are drawn as built-up (holes under the threshold are filled).
